_doc: Plain-language scoreboard for the C10 problem (made-up multi-word names), shown by tools/dashboard_report.py. The program session updates it at every result and close-out: add a results row, refresh current/queue, rewrite the brief in plain words. Scores are held-out reworded questions answered exactly right, out of 72. Full detail lives in CORPUS; this file only points there.
brief: We are trying to teach the model made-up names (like a project codename) so it can recall them when a question is worded differently. Ordinary facts already work (about 69 of 72); made-up two-word names do not: the usual method gets about 9 to 14 of 72, our best write method about 40, and the goal is 61. Step 4 (let each fact pick its own layer) did not help and is not taken forward. Step 5 asks whether training that same small part of the model can reach the goal at all: the repeat run scored 70 to 71 of 72, but its final self-check tripped on a rounding bug, so there is no official reading yet.

current.what: Step 5 ceiling test, repeat run: STOPPED, needs your ruling. Training and scoring finished (new seed 71 of 72; same-seed retrain identical), but a rounding bug in the last self-check blocked the official reading. The recommended fix uses no GPU.
